subject: Action required: Temporary traffic shift & safe-harbor steps for impacted regions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Action required: Temporary traffic shift & safe-harbor steps for impacted regions

Hi Susan / ACME Ops —

Quick summary: we are observing a regional control-plane failover affecting a subset of hosts in EU-central and APAC-south that is increasing tail latency for a small percentage of your calls. Our mitigation is a targeted traffic steer (reroute) to nearby healthy POPs while we stabilize connectivity. This message outlines the safe-harbor steps for you to opt into the temporary reroute and what to expect.

What we are asking you to do now (3-minute checklist):
- Confirm you want Redwood to proactively steer affected requests for ACME tenants (reply with YES).
- If you prefer, set DNS TTL to 30s for the next 6 hours (instructions below).
- If you rely on strict regional data residency, reply with "NO - need manual review" and we will open an exception path.

How steering works (brief):
- We will apply a routing policy that prefers US-west for US traffic, EU-west for EU traffic, and APAC-east for APAC traffic.
- Sticky sessions and KV cache will be primed; you may see a small rise in cold-start token usage for ~5 minutes after cutover.
- We will keep latency SLO targets and monitor error-rate regressions; if any customer-level regression appears we will roll back immediately.

Operational details (internal):
- Runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-incident-runbook
- Ops pager: ben_carter on-call; Naomi to monitor cache warmup telemetry.

Attachments: reroute-checklist.pdf, runbook-traffic-shift-20290807.md

Expect a follow-up note once steering is live (approx +10 minutes).

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Rishi —

Confirming: YES, please proceed with the proactive steer for ACME tenants. We do not require strict regional residency for the sessions affected by this issue. A couple of quick Qs:
- Can you confirm whether embeddings requests will also be steered? We have a background job that bursts embeddings during mornings.
- If we see any model-quality change, what is the rollback SLA?

Thanks,
Susan
VP Product, ACME Corp.
ACME Ops: ops@acmecorp.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-07T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action required: Temporary traffic shift & safe-harbor steps for impacted regions

Susan — great, thanks for the quick YES. Short answers:
- Embeddings: yes — our routing policy includes embeddings and reranks. We will tag ACME’s tenant id and steer all model classes used by your account for the impacted POPs.
- Rollback SLA: immediate rollback if you or telemetry trigger any of the following: >0.5% absolute error-rate increase, sustained >250ms p95 latency regression for 3 consecutive minutes, or any measurable drop in model quality on your provided prompts. We will proactively rollback if thresholds meet.

Planned sequence (timeline):
- +00m: Apply steward routing policy to ACME tenant (non-disruptive, traffic mirrored for validation).
- +5m: Start steer at 10% incremental steps over 10 minutes.
- +20m: Reach 100% steer barring regressions.

Operational notes: Naomi will post a short telemetry snapshot after +15 minutes. If you want a rollback, reply: ROLLBACK and we will revert within 120s.

—Rishi

Subject: telemetry snapshot — steer at 30%

Team —

Steer is live at 30% for ACME. Early observations:
- Request error rate: stable (no customer-visible 5xx).
- p95 latency: EU traffic p95 improved from 640ms to 280ms after reroute; APAC p95 improved from 720ms to 310ms.
- Embedding job: small cold-start bump in tokens for 6 minutes, then normalizing.

Customer impact: none reported so far from ACME. Continuing to ramp to 100% on the planned cadence.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-07T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update: traffic steer complete and post-incident next steps

Susan / ACME Ops —

Final update for the active window: we completed the traffic steer to healthy POPs (100%) at ~09:52 PDT and held for validation. Metrics summary:
- Steer completion: 100% at +40m (no regressions detected).
- Latency: EU p95 now ~270ms; APAC p95 ~305ms; US p95 stable.
- Errors: no ACME customer-visible 5xx spikes.

Post-incident follow-ups (what we will do, and what we recommend):
- Redwood will keep the routing policy in place as a protective measure for the next 24 hours; we will revert automatically unless we detect full recovery of the regional control-plane (expected within 12–36 hours).
- Recommended for ACME: no action required while we hold the steer. If you want us to revert earlier, reply: ROLLBACK.
- We will provide a short postmortem by EOD tomorrow that includes timeline, root cause, and improvement actions (runbook updates, kernel selection tweak).

Attachments: runbook-traffic-shift-20290807.md (contains opt-in steps, DNS instructions, and validation queries.)

Thanks for the quick coordination — we’ll follow up with the postmortem and a brief recorded run-through if you’d like a walk-through.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
